blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Before he was king, David lived in the wilderness with about six hundred men. They camped near the flocks of a rich man named Nabal and kept his shepherds safe. When it was time to shear the sheep, David sent ten young men to Nabal to ask kindly for whatever he could spare.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Nabal sent them away with insults. Who is David, he said. When David heard it, he told four hundred of his men to strap on their swords.

verses.text: But one of the young men told Abigail, Nabal’s wife, saying, Behold, David sent messengers out of the wilderness to salute our master; and he railed on them.

verses.text: But the men were very good unto us, and we were not hurt, neither missed we any thing, as long as we were conversant with them, when we were in the fields:

verses.text: Now therefore know and consider what thou wilt do; for evil is determined against our master, and against all his household: for he is such a son of Belial, that a man cannot speak to him.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: The servant did not go to Nabal. He went to Abigail. He knew she would listen, and he knew she was wise.

verses.text: Then Abigail made haste, and took two hundred loaves, and two bottles of wine, and five sheep ready dressed, and five measures of parched corn, and an hundred clusters of raisins, and two hundred cakes of figs, and laid them on asses.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: She did not stop to argue or to wring her hands. She loaded up bread and wine, meat and grain, raisins and figs, and she moved.

verses.text: And she said unto her servants, Go on before me; behold, I come after you. But she told not her husband Nabal.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: David was angry, and his anger was carrying him toward something terrible. He meant to wipe out every man in Nabal's house before morning.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: The name Nabal means fool. Abigail did not pretend her husband had done right. She took the blame on herself and asked David to hear her out.

verses.text: Now therefore, my lord, as the LORD liveth, and as thy soul liveth, seeing the LORD hath withholden thee from coming to shed blood, and from avenging thyself with thine own hand, now let thine enemies, and they that seek evil to my lord, be as Nabal.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: She reminded David who he was. He fought the LORD's battles. He did not need to fight this one. One day he would be king, and she did not want him to carry this blood with him when that day came.

verses.text: And David said to Abigail, Blessed be the LORD God of Israel, which sent thee this day to meet me:

verses.text: And blessed be thy advice, and blessed be thou, which hast kept me this day from coming to shed blood, and from avenging myself with mine own hand.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: David did not say, you are right. He said, blessed be the LORD who sent you. He saw God's hand in the woman standing in the road.

verses.text: So David received of her hand that which she had brought him, and said unto her, Go up in peace to thine house; see, I have hearkened to thy voice, and have accepted thy person.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: One woman, a few donkeys loaded with bread, and a few honest words. That was enough to turn four hundred swords around. Abigail did not have an army. She had wisdom, and the courage to step into the road at the right moment. God used it to keep a future king from doing a wrong he could never take back.

first_reader.note: Written by Claude in the landing session, then Claude's pastor and cultural read.

pastor.note: Faithful to 1 Sam 25:14-35 (v22 and v34's coarse phrase left out by choosing verses, not by changing them); the set-up (vv 2-13) told plainly from the text; credit to God as David gives it in v32.

cultural.note: Abigail shown as wise and brave, a woman whose word turns an army; Nabal named a fool only as the text and his wife do.
